title: T1: deployment census of M, the ciphertexts decapsulable under one ML-KEM encapsulation key
validity_reason: Documentary census. Every row cites a primary specification that was fetched over the network in this task, with HTTP status, byte count, SHA-256 and UTC retrieval timestamp recorded per source below. No row rests on recollection: each quoted clause was located by full-text search in the retrieved artifact, and each 'M not stated' finding names the search terms that establish the absence. One source (NSA CNSA 2.0) could not be retrieved and is recorded as an acquisition failure, never as a specification that states no bound.

certificate.reason: Pure documentary measurement. No discrete-log solve, no factor-base relation, no lattice computation, no solver of any kind was run. There is nothing to certify. Integrity rests instead on per-source SHA-256 and HTTP status, which make every citation independently re-fetchable and checkable.

measured_vs_modeled: Every number in census.md and census.json is a MEASURED property of a retrieved document (a stated M, a stated cryptoperiod, a row count, a search hit count). Nothing is modeled. In particular no cryptoperiod or certificate validity period was converted into a ciphertext count, because that conversion needs a decapsulation rate that no retrieved specification supplies.

claims.scope: M only, as stated by published specifications. No quantity derived from M appears in any deliverable: no log2 M, no G, no block size, no bit figure. The task card forbids them and the deliverables were scanned to confirm their absence.

rule12_status: AGENTS.md rule 12 is UNMET and UNWAIVED, inherited from GOAL-MLKEM-003/004. Nothing in this task changes, or treats as corrected, any EV-MLKEM-* record or KN-* entry. No ML-KEM break claim. This is defensive vetting of FIPS 203.

steps: Resolved current Internet-Draft revisions through the IETF Datatracker API (https://datatracker.ietf.org/api/v1/doc/document/<name>/?format=json) rather than guessing a version number, and recorded the resolved rev.
Fetched each source with curl, recording HTTP status, effective URL, byte count, SHA-256 and UTC timestamp for every attempt including failures.

Extracted text from the three NIST PDFs with pypdf 6.14.2 in an isolated venv (the system pypdf import fails: the distro `cryptography` package is broken with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '_cffi_backend').
Located the M-bounding clause in each source by full-text search, and for every 'not stated' finding ran and recorded the negative search terms.
Emitted census.json and census.md from ONE row table in a single builder script, so the machine-readable rows and the rendered table cannot disagree.

draft_revisions_resolved._note: Datatracker reports rfc: None for every one of these, i.e. none is yet an RFC. The IANA TLS Supported Groups registry lists X25519MLKEM768 (4588) against 'RFC-ietf-tls-ecdhe-mlkem-05', the RFC Editor queue form of the same draft; recorded precisely rather than called an RFC.

headline.distribution_sentence: Across the 14 deployment-mode rows sourced here, 6 fix M = 1 (R09, R12, R14, R20, R21, R22) and the remaining 8 state no count bound at all (R06, R10, R15, R16, R17, R18, R19, R23) -- and the largest numeric M stated by ANY of the 24 rows, ephemeral or static, is 1, because every static row bounds the key in time or by a rate-limiting SHOULD and never by a number of ciphertexts.
headline.does_any_standardised_mode_state_M_above: No retrieved specification states any numeric M greater than 1, so none states an M above 2^20. Symmetrically, and this must be reported with equal weight: none of the 8 count-unstated modes forbids one either. The absence is an absence of a stated number in both directions; it is not a sourced ceiling and must not be read as one.
headline.structural_finding: For every static or reused row, the specification bounds the key in TIME (certificate validity, a 1-to-2-year cryptoperiod, a rotation RECOMMENDATION) or by a rate-limiting SHOULD, and never by a count of ciphertexts. The one normative delegation of a count -- draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design-16 Sec. 2, 'the number of reuses of a KEM public key abides by any bounds in the specification of the KEM' -- terminates at FIPS 203, which states no such bound.
headline.interpretation_boundary: This is an Executor observation set. Whether a count-unstated static mode should be treated as bounded, unbounded, or unknown for the purpose of C1 is a judgement for the Reviewer, Red Team and Coordinator. The Executor does not make it here.

controls.reason: There is no contrast, comparator, surrogate or ablation in this task. It is a single-arm documentary census: no measured quantity, no treatment, no parameter that could be increased to destroy a signal, and therefore no null object of the same shape to build. Stated here as the task card directs, rather than inventing a null in order to look rigorous.
controls.what_stands_in_for_a_control: The negative full-text search. Every row whose M is recorded as 'not stated' names in census.md the exact search terms used to establish the absence, so a reviewer can re-run them against the SHA-256-pinned source and falsify the row if a bound exists. Key negative searches run: FIPS 203 for cryptoperiod|number of queries/decapsulations/encapsulations/ciphertexts/uses|multi-user|multi-target|at most 2 (0 hits); SP 800-227 for the same plus 'limit the number' (0 hits); PKCS#11 v3.2 for CKA_USAGE|usage count|usage limit (0 hits); RFC 9420 for ML-KEM|MLKEM (0 hits).

The census includes rows the task card did not enumerate (SSH draft-ietf-sshm-mlkem-hybrid-kex, IKEv2 draft-ietf-ipsecme-ikev2-mlkem, CMS RFC 9629 + draft-ietf-lamps-cms-kyber, Signal PQXDH, NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5, draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design, draft-sfluhrer-cfrg-ml-kem-security-considerations, standalone TLS ML-KEM). This is an expansion of coverage, not a substitution: every source the card named was attempted, and the only one not retrieved is the CNSA 2.0 advisory recorded as an acquisition failure. Note that SSH, IKEv2 and PQXDH one-time prekeys all ADD to the ephemeral (M = 1) share, so the expansion does not flatter the large-M side.

anomalies.observation: RFC 9420 (MLS) as published standardises NO ML-KEM cipher suite: its Sec. 17.1 registry holds only DHKEM(X25519/X448/P-256/P-384/P-521) suites, and full-text search for 'ML-KEM'/'MLKEM' returns 0 hits.
anomalies.why_recorded: The task card lists MLS as a source of M. The KeyPackage mechanism is real and is censused (R09, R10), but calling it a standardised ML-KEM deployment today would overstate it. Recorded as scope_note R11.

anomalies.observation: ML-KEM cannot instantiate HPKE's auth or auth_psk modes at all: draft-connolly-cfrg-hpke-mlkem-04 Sec. 1.2 and 3.7 state that ML-KEM 'does not support the static-static key agreement needed by ... their (optional) authenticated modes' and supplies no AuthEncap/AuthDecap.
anomalies.why_recorded: The task card asks for HPKE base/PSK/auth modes. Two of those three carry no ML-KEM M by construction. Recorded as scope_note R07 rather than as an empty row.

anomalies.observation: The only normative delegation of a numeric reuse bound found anywhere in the survey -- draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design-16 Sec. 2, repeated verbatim in draft-connolly-tls-mlkem-key-agreement-05 Sec. 6.2 -- points at 'any bounds in the specification of the KEM', and FIPS 203 contains no such bound.
anomalies.why_recorded: It is the load-bearing chain for the whole census: the standards system does attempt to bound M, and the pointer dead-ends. This is a finding about the specification stack, not about ML-KEM's security.

anomalies.observation: ECH is the one surveyed mode whose own privacy goal actively rewards a LARGER M: draft-ietf-tls-esni-25 Sec. 10.3 warns that 'Rotating too frequently limits the client anonymity set' while Sec. 10.10.5 only RECOMMENDS regular rotation. Even there, no number is stated.
anomalies.why_recorded: It is the natural place a large deployed M would appear, and it is recorded as such so that no reader concludes the census failed to look where the answer would be. It is still count-unstated.

anomalies.observation: Signal PQXDH is a genuinely deployed system with exactly the one-time/last-resort structure of interest (R22 M = 1, R23 count-unstated), but its specification names the pqkem parameter as 'e.g. Crystals-Kyber-1024', not FIPS 203 ML-KEM.
anomalies.why_recorded: Included for its M-bounding mechanism with the mismatch stated in the row caveat, so it is never read as an ML-KEM conformance statement.

completion_gate.every_row_check_method: census.json rows all carry non-empty spec, section, bounding_mechanism, m, m_derivation, citation, retrieval_date and source_sha256; verified programmatically after write
completion_gate.distribution_sentence_check: The single distribution sentence names the ephemeral (M = 1) count and the largest stated M in the same sentence. No maximum is quoted anywhere in any deliverable without the ephemeral share beside it. This is the GOAL-MLKEM-004 batch 4 DEF-7 defect the card names, and it is guarded structurally: the sentence is generated from the row counts, not written by hand.
completion_gate.derived_quantity_scan: census.md and census.json were scanned for 'log2', 'log_2', 'bits of', 'core-SVP', 'beta' and a bare G comparison. The only matches are the four explicit statements that no such quantity appears (census.md lines 10, 11, 110; census.json 'scope_restriction'). A literal '2^' search returns five matches: three '2^20' occurrences restating the task's own question (census.md lines 23 and 25, census.json 'does_any_standardised_mode_state_M_above_2_20'), and two occurrences of the bare string '2^' inside row R24's list of negative full-text search terms (census.md line 77, census.json rows[23].m_derivation). No deliverable contains a computed bit figure, a log2 of anything, or any quantity derived from M.
